blocks.intro: In July 2011, record rainfall flooded basements across Ravenswood.

items.body: The lowest living space floods first.
If it only happens in heavy rain, the city sewer is full. On dry days, your line is blocked.
A backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/chicago-ravenswood/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps sewer water out.

blocks.h2: When a Garden Unit Floods With Sewage
blocks.body: If someone lives in the garden unit, a backup is more than a wet basement. Get the residents out of the affected rooms, ask the upstairs units to stop using water and call us. Once we clear the line, a restoration company should clean and dry the space before anyone moves back in. Then talk to us about protection. For a below-grade apartment, an overhead sewer or backflow valve is often worth it after one bad backup.

blocks.h2: Sewer Backup Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Why does the garden unit flood in heavy rain?
items.answer: Chicago's sewers carry rain and wastewater together. In a heavy storm, they fill and push back into the lowest drains.

items.q: What protects a garden unit best?
items.preview: An overhead sewer for repeat backups.
items.answer: For repeat backups, an overhead sewer. For lighter risk, a backflow valve or standpipe.

items.q: Is a sewer backup covered by insurance?
items.answer: Many policies need a sewer backup rider. Check with your agent.

items.q: Do you clean up after a backup?
items.preview: We fix the plumbing. A restoration company cleans up.
items.answer: We clear the line and repair the cause. A restoration company handles cleanup and drying.

items.q: Can the upstairs units keep using water?
items.preview: No, not until the line is clear.
items.answer: No. Their water drains through the same line and ends up downstairs.

items.q: How much does sewer backup service cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what caused it and how we reach the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
